claims.statement: Every even natural number n > 2 is the sum of two primes.
claims.notes: The target. Verified computationally to 4*10^18 (Oliveira e Silva, Herzog, Pardi 2014) — verify citation before using as a number.

claims.statement: Every odd natural number n > 5 is the sum of three primes.
claims.hypothesis: GRH + 5 axioms in WeakGoldbach/Analytic.lean (R_total, M_coeff, grh_arc_error_bound, major_arc_main_term_lower_bound, prime_power_subtraction_bound) + binaryGoldbach_4e18 + certified_prime_ladder_1e22
claims.notes: Cloned repo claims GRH-conditional proof for odd N>=7 with a finite ladder 4e18->1e22. The Lean theorem derives from 17 declared axioms (audit finding 2026-11-26); NOT checked. Python interval verifiers for constants PASS.

claims.statement: E(X) <= 2,000,000 sqrt(X) (log X)^3, where E(X) counts even n in [4,X] not a sum of two primes; hence E(X)/X -> 0.
claims.hypothesis: GRH + 10 axioms in WeakGoldbach/BinaryExceptional.lean (R2_total, M2_coeff, T_trunc, U_tail, S2_series, J_int, grh_binary_arc_L2_bound, binary_singular_integral_bounds, binary_singular_series_bounds, binary_prime_power_bound) + binaryGoldbach_4e18
claims.notes: Almost-all result, not pointwise. Derives from declared axioms (audit 2026-11-26); NOT checked. Python interval verifier PASS.

claims.statement: Binary Goldbach verified for every even 4 <= n <= 4*10^18.
claims.source: Oliveira e Silva, Herzog, Pardi (2014), cited by cloned repo
claims.notes: Literature claim, not independently re-run. Do not mark checked until we have a checked certificate or a run we performed.

claims.statement: Every sufficiently large even n is p + P2 (prime plus product of at most two primes) — Chen's (1+2) theorem.
claims.notes: Unconditional published theorem. Candidate for formalization route.

claims.statement: Li–Liu (1+1.9): eventual weighted count D19(N) > c*N/log^2(N) giving p + q with prime q and r in {1,prime}, r^10 <= q^9.
claims.source: arXiv:2606.05224 (Li–Liu); discussed in cloned repo's research docs
claims.notes: Published 2026 result, not verified by us. Potential blocker/route.

claims.notes: 4999 explicit prime-pair witnesses generated by src/gen_cert.py (sieve), each primality proved by norm_num; lake build exit 0 (95s). NOT the full conjecture.

claims.notes: Kernel build exit 0. Detects primes via Liouville on cube-root-rough integers; corrects (1-mu)/2 misweighting of prime squares. Supports one-sided reductions (8)/(9); does not prove them.
